- Bus data from TTC Municipal fleet data from the CEO's report for December, 2022: https://cdn.ttc.ca/-/media/Project/TTC/DevProto/Documents/Home/Public-Meetings/Board/2022/December-8/2_CEO_Report_December_2022_Update.pdf?rev=4c8a112fc4f846ea9151e19856009dea&hash=7CEAF5C90B46CD3137E08CE992515DA7

- Taxis data from 2022, from the City of Toronto's Municipal Licenses and Standards Division. Reported fuel sources for all fleet types are: Electric fleet is battery electric (BEV), hybrid fleet is gas/electric (HEV), and plug in hybrid fleet is gas/battery (PHEV).

- Private electric vehicle (EV) data from the Ontario Ministry of Transportation (MTO) classifies electric vehicles as either battery electric vehicles (BEV) or plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEV). Therefore, we are unable to report the number of HEVs, although it is included within the total electric fleet size for private vehicles. column19:
Emissions for transport modes have previously been estimated by applying the shares estimated from a bottom-up modelling exercise in 2018. These are scaled to match the fuel sales derived total emissions.

In the 2023 inventory, the methodologies for both the bottom-up modelling and allocation of fuel sales to on-road transport have been updated, resulting in notable changes. A vehicle parc model disaggregated by mode was built using the LEAP platform to estimate transport share from the bottom-up. In addition, the fuel attribution methodology was completely overhauled by a service provider under a contract to improve the GHG data systems. Insights from an interview with the local refinery provided insights into how fuel was allocated to different sectors. 

In total the petroleum fuel consumption estimate was 20% lower than 2022 but this number is only known to around that level of accuracy because the regional attribution of fuel sales is determined by survey of wholesalers not retailers and substantial leakage across boundaries occurs.

The 2023 estimate for minibus taxis mode share has dropped somewhat more than the total. The vehicle parc stock model showed a much higher share of diesel fueling than previously thought, shifting the fuel economy substantially. The calibration of this model also reduced mileage assumptions. These assumptions will be reviewed as the new methodology matures. 

Taxis (4.6.5) includes minibus taxis (16 - 35 seats) which are privately owned but are allocated routes by the provincial transport authority and account for a 30 - 40% passenger km mode share.

Fleet size figures are 2023 data year to align with GHG inventory.

Transportasi Darat (kendaraan bermotor): ± 362.790 ton CO₂e (96%)

Moda darat adalah penyumbang emisi terbesar dari sektor transportasi di Manado.

Laut berkontribusi kecil tetapi signifikan untuk kegiatan logistik dan perikanan.

Total emisi transportasi ini menyumbang hampir setengah dari total emisi Kota Manado pada tahun dasar.
